requirements.text: create a new incident with high impact, and urgency with the description 'Payroll Service Total Outage' and assign it to her (a total outage of the 'Payroll Service', reported by Stephanie Todd)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_006' AND description = 'Payroll Service Total Outage' AND service_offering = 'SVCOFF_002' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND assigned_to = 'USER_006' AND status = 'new'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100); the only incident the task creates

Stephanie Todd is USER_006 (active agent, ORG_001, LOC_001), the only user with that name; she reported the outage, so she is caller_id (policy 3.1: the user affected), and 'assign it to her' sets assigned_to
'high impact, and urgency' read as impact high and urgency high; priority critical from the policy 3.1 matrix; status new from the policy default

'Payroll Service' is the exact name of no service or offering: Global Payroll (SVC_002) and its standard offering SVCOFF_002 are the operational match; Payroll - Ad Hoc (SVCOFF_019) and the Payroll QA environment are in status ready
the service column is not tested separately: the offering fixes the service
category is mandatory in the schema but the request and policy fix no value, so it is not a cell; the original check's software is dropped
the text goes in description, as the request says; short_description is mandatory but its wording is not fixed, so it is not a cell; the policy's opened_by has no column

disagreement: A tests assignment_group (IS NULL OR GROUP_002, from policy 3.2 and her one group membership), B does not; dropped because the request names no group and policy 3.2 binds only on a specified group, and a disjunction is not a cell predicate

requirements.text: She also reported that she has completed her previous assigned ticket. Make sure that this also is updated into the system.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_095' AND status = 'resolved' AND resolution_code IS NOT NULL AND resolution_notes IS NOT NULL AND resolution_notes <> ''
assumptions: INC_095 'Teams Lag' (status new) is the only incident assigned to USER_006, so it is her previous assigned ticket
'completed' means status resolved: new to resolved is a valid transition (policy 3.3) and the message to Stephanie says the ticket has been resolved; closed is reached automatically 72 hours later
policy 3.3 makes resolution_code and resolution_notes mandatory for resolved; neither value is fixed by the request, so both are tested as present
disagreement: form: resolution_notes is one COALESCE expression in A and a list of two predicates in B; the list is kept (the cell rule); same rows

notes: Merged from two independent passes. Both anchored the two notifications to NOTIF_031 (regional manager) and NOTIF_032 (Stephanie) in request order; rewritten as selectors on incident and recipient because the task creates two rows in that table and the request fixes no sending order, so an agent that sends Stephanie's first still passes. disagreement: A's assignment_group cell on the new incident (IS NULL OR GROUP_002, from policy 3.2; B had none); dropped because the request names no group and policy 3.2 binds only on a specified group, and a disjunction is not a cell predicate. disagreement: value: Stephanie's message is a LIKE containment in A and exact equality in B; the containment is kept, as the original check reads it. disagreement: form: resolution_notes is one COALESCE expression in A and a list of two predicates in B; the list is kept (the cell rule). disagreement: form: the regional-manager stay's cells mirror its SQL in A and contradict it in B; A's form is kept. disagreement: disposition: Previous Ticket Resolved is repaired in A and kept in B; kept, since the check is wrong in no value and only gains the policy's resolution_code cell. The regional manager is decided from the seed (Robin Monroe, USER_031, the only manager-role user at Stephanie's location LOC_001), not from the request, which never names him; the group manager_id of GROUP_002, Christina Oliver (USER_002), is a reporter in ORG_002. 'Payroll Service' is the exact name of no service or offering; Global Payroll (SVC_002) and its standard offering SVCOFF_002 are the operational match, with Payroll - Ad Hoc (SVCOFF_019) and the QA environment in status ready; the policy's ambiguity rule could instead have the agent halt and list the candidates, which the benchmark does not expect. The acting user Karen Watkins (USER_039) is an admin in ORG_001; INC_095 sits in ORG_011 though assigned to a user in ORG_001, which the policy does not address. Least sure: dropping the assignment_group cell, which encodes a real policy constraint (she is a member of GROUP_002 only) that the request leaves open.
